steps.intent: Our objective is to enforce the automatic trigger clause in paragraph 28 of resolution 2397 (2017) following the DPRK's brazen ICBM launches, constraining Pyongyang's revenue and fuel supply for its weapons programmes and targeting illicit cyber activities. We anticipate strong resistance and potential vetoes from China and the Russian Federation, who argue that sanctions exacerbate humanitarian suffering and that the Council should instead offer sanctions relief to encourage dialogue. To maximize support among elected members and isolate obstructionists, we have included clear humanitarian safeguards, streamlined exemption procedures, and explicit commitments to unconditional diplomatic re-engagement.

messages.Albania: Albania fully supports this draft resolution presented by the United States. The DPRK's continuous, reckless ICBM launches and defiance of Council resolutions demand a firm, unified, and decisive response from this organ, in line with the trigger provisions of resolution 2397 (2017). We stand ready to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Brazil: Brazil condemns the DPRK's recent ICBM launches in the strongest terms as flagrant violations of Council resolutions and a serious threat to international peace and security. While we support decisive Council action to uphold the non-proliferation architecture, we must ensure that measures do not exacerbate the fragile humanitarian and public health situation of the DPRK population. We also urge the penholder to emphasize diplomatic engagement and de-escalation as the indispensable path to complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization.
messages.China: China strongly opposes the introduction of additional punitive sanctions against the DPRK, which will only aggravate tensions, close the door to dialogue, and severely worsen the humanitarian situation of the DPRK people amid the current COVID-19 outbreak. Sanctions are not an end in themselves, and blind reliance on pressure without addressing the DPRK's legitimate and reasonable security concerns has repeatedly proven ineffective. If the penholder insists on railroading a text imposing new sanctions rather than fostering conditions for the resumption of talks, China will have no choice but to vote against it.
messages.France: France fully supports the draft resolution presented by the United States and commends its leadership on this critical issue. Following the DPRK's reckless ICBM launches on 24 March and 25 May, the Security Council cannot remain silent in the face of such flagrant violations of international non-proliferation obligations. We support strengthening the sanctions regime, including the activation of the snapback mechanism on petroleum imports under resolution 2397 (2017) and measures addressing illicit cyber activities, to advance our collective objective of complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization.
messages.Gabon: Gabon strongly condemns the repeated ballistic missile tests conducted by the DPRK, which violate Security Council resolutions and threaten regional and international peace and security. While we support decisive action to uphold the non-proliferation regime and enforce Council decisions, we must ensure that enhanced measures do not compound the suffering of the North Korean civilian population, especially in light of the severe COVID-19 outbreak. We also urge all parties to keep channels of dialogue open toward a peaceful, political resolution.
messages.Ghana: Ghana views the DPRK's repeated ICBM launches as a clear and unacceptable violation of Security Council resolutions that directly triggers the Council's commitments under paragraph 28 of resolution 2397 (2017). While we support the draft resolution to uphold the global non-proliferation architecture, we must ensure that tightened measures do not exacerbate the hardships of the civilian population, especially in light of the unfolding COVID-19 outbreak in the country. We also stress that sanctions are not an end in themselves and must be accompanied by renewed diplomatic efforts toward peaceful denuclearization.
messages.India: India firmly condemns the recent series of ICBM launches by the DPRK as flagrant violations of Security Council resolutions that jeopardize peace and stability in the region and beyond. We support Council action in line with paragraph 28 of resolution 2397 (2017), while underscoring the pressing need to address illicit proliferation networks and linkages associated with the DPRK's programmes. We also emphasize that sanctions must not aggravate the humanitarian situation of the DPRK's civilian population, especially amid emerging public health challenges.
messages.Ireland: Ireland strongly supports this draft resolution and the robust, united response it provides to the DPRK's escalatory and unlawful intercontinental ballistic missile launches, which represent a grave threat to international peace and security and the non-proliferation architecture. In light of the precarious humanitarian and public health situation on the ground, we suggest explicitly ensuring that the 1718 Committee's exemption mechanism effectively facilitates critical humanitarian and medical supplies. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text and urge all Council members to support its adoption.
messages.Kenya: Kenya strongly condemns the DPRK's recurrent ICBM launches, which represent a dangerous escalation and a clear violation of Security Council resolutions. While we support the draft resolution and the Council's resolve on non-proliferation, we underline the imperative to safeguard the civilian population from unintended adverse humanitarian consequences, especially given recent public health vulnerabilities. We also stress that sanctions must be accompanied by active diplomatic engagement and dialogue toward lasting peace and denuclearization on the Korean Peninsula.
messages.Mexico: Mexico condemns in the strongest terms the recent ICBM launches by the DPRK, which represent grave violations of Security Council resolutions and undermine the international non-proliferation architecture. While we support decisive Council action pursuant to resolution 2397 (2017), we must ensure that new measures do not exacerbate the precarious humanitarian situation in the DPRK, especially given the ongoing COVID-19 health emergency. We urge the penholder to reinforce humanitarian exemption mechanisms and maintain an unwavering commitment to diplomatic dialogue.
messages.Norway: Norway strongly supports the draft resolution and condemns in the strongest terms the DPRK's repeated intercontinental ballistic missile launches, which represent a serious threat to international peace and security and flagrantly violate Council resolutions. The Council must uphold its own decisions and respond decisively to the triggering of paragraph 28 of resolution 2397 (2017). At the same time, we attach great importance to minimizing adverse humanitarian impacts on the civilian population, and we propose a minor reference to the current COVID-19 outbreak in the DPRK to ensure humanitarian and medical exemptions can be processed expeditiously.
messages.Russian Federation: Russia categorically opposes the introduction of new sanctions against the DPRK, which have proven to be an ineffective and dangerous dead end that exacerbates the humanitarian situation of the North Korean population. Pushing forward with an exclusively punitive approach while ignoring Pyongyang's legitimate security concerns and the absence of reciprocal steps from Washington undermines prospects for political-diplomatic engagement. The Council must shift its focus toward genuine dialogue and de-escalation rather than ratcheting up pressure.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates firmly supports this draft resolution in response to the DPRK's repeated and dangerous ICBM launches, which directly violate Security Council resolutions and threaten regional and international security. The Council must uphold its own credibility and act in accordance with the trigger provisions established in resolution 2397 (2017). We also welcome the clear safeguards in paragraph 8 regarding humanitarian exemptions, which are vital given the acute humanitarian and public health challenges facing the civilian population.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports this timely and necessary draft resolution circulated by the United States. Following the DPRK's dangerous and unprecedented barrage of ballistic missile launches, including multiple ICBM tests in direct defiance of international law, the Council must uphold its own commitment under paragraph 28 of resolution 2397 (2017) and respond with resolve. We fully endorse the targeted strengthening of sanctions, including the reduction of petroleum caps and measures to curb illicit cyber activities, and urge all Council members to vote in favour.

steps.summary: The United States maintains the draft resolution in its current form, upholding the Council's explicit commitment under resolution 2397 (2017) to respond decisively to the DPRK's escalatory ICBM launches. The United States rejects demands from China and Russia to dismantle key sanctions provisions and grant premature sanctions relief, which would reward unlawful weapons proliferation and undermine international security. With overwhelming support from thirteen Council members across regional groups, the United States proceeds to put the resolution to a vote.

before.China:
Mr. President,

China has always maintained that maintaining peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula and realizing its complete denuclearization serves the common interests of all parties and the international community.

The situation on the Korean Peninsula has developed to where it is today primarily because the denuclearization measures taken by the DPRK in 2018 have not been met with reciprocal actions from the United States, and the legitimate and reasonable concerns of the DPRK have not been addressed. The dialogue between the DPRK and the United States has been stalled for a prolonged period, and distrust between the parties has deepened.

Under the current circumstances, additional sanctions will not help resolve the problem. On the contrary, ramping up sanctions will only lead to further escalation, exacerbate the humanitarian situation and the hardships faced by the DPRK people—especially in the face of the emerging COVID-19 epidemic in the country—and shut the door to dialogue. What is needed now is dialogue, restraint, and concrete actions to address the legitimate security concerns of all parties, rather than simply resorting to pressure and sanctions.

China and Russia jointly proposed a draft resolution aimed at easing sanctions affecting the humanitarian and livelihood needs of the DPRK people and creating conditions to encourage the resumption of dialogue. Regrettably, the penholder chose to push for a vote on a draft resolution that only tightens sanctions and creates confrontation, completely ignoring the reasonable proposals of China and other Council members.

Piling on new sanctions against the DPRK will only prove counterproductive. China has no choice but to vote against this draft resolution.
before.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Today, the Security Council must fulfill its responsibility to uphold international peace and security. Yesterday, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea launched three ballistic missiles, including an intercontinental ballistic missile. This comes on the heels of the DPRK’s March 24 ICBM launch and an unprecedented barrage of more than 20 ballistic missile launches already this year. Each and every one of these launches constitutes a flagrant violation of multiple unanimously adopted Security Council resolutions.

The DPRK's unlawful weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programs pose an undeniable threat to regional stability and the global non-proliferation regime. The Council cannot remain silent in the face of such repeated, brazen provocations. 

In resolution 2397, which this Council adopted unanimously in 2017, we committed to act. Specifically, in paragraph 28, the Council decided that if the DPRK were to launch an ICBM, we would take action to further restrict petroleum exports to the DPRK. That trigger was activated. Today’s draft resolution directly honors that commitment. It restricts refined petroleum and crude oil supplies, curbs illicit cyber activities that fund these unlawful weapons programs, and strengthens sanctions enforcement, while ensuring swift and uninterrupted humanitarian exceptions to help the vulnerable people of North Korea, particularly in light of their ongoing COVID-19 outbreak.

The United States has repeatedly offered to engage in dialogue with Pyongyang without preconditions, but our offers have been met only with silence and new missile launches. Council inaction is not an option; it only emboldens the DPRK to continue its dangerous escalations. 

We urge every member of this Council to stand united, uphold our own words and resolutions, and vote in favor of this resolution.

Thank you.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania voted in favour of the draft resolution presented by the United States, and we deeply regret that the Security Council failed to adopt it today due to the veto cast by two permanent members.

Today’s vote was a critical test of the Council’s credibility, responsibility, and resolve. Faced with the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s repeated, deliberate, and dangerous escalation—including an unprecedented barrage of ballistic missile launches this year and multiple tests of intercontinental ballistic missiles, most recently just yesterday—the Council had a clear duty to act. 

Each of these launches represents a blatant violation of multiple Security Council resolutions and a direct challenge to the international non-proliferation architecture, threatening regional and global peace and security. In resolution 2397 (2017), adopted unanimously, this Council committed itself to further restrict petroleum exports to the DPRK if it were to conduct another ICBM launch. The draft resolution before us today was the direct and logical consequence of that very commitment. It was not an escalation; it was the Council fulfilling its own word.

Instead, by shielding Pyongyang from the consequences of its unlawful actions, the Council has sent the worst possible message. It signals to the DPRK that it can continue to violate international law, pursue weapons of mass destruction, and threaten its neighbours with complete impunity. Silence and inaction in the face of such continuous provocation do not de-escalate tensions; they only embolden the regime to accelerate its nuclear and ballistic missile programmes.

We also reject the argument that this resolution would have worsened the humanitarian situation of the North Korean people. The text contained clear and robust humanitarian exemptions, specifically tailored to address public health needs, particularly in light of the COVID-19 outbreak. The true cause of the suffering of the North Korean people lies in the regime’s cynical decision to divert vital national resources toward its unlawful military adventures and weapons of mass destruction.

Albania remains firmly committed to a peaceful, diplomatic, and political solution leading to the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula. We call on the DPRK to immediately cease all destabilizing actions, abide by its international obligations, comply with Security Council resolutions, and return to meaningful dialogue. 

Thank you.
after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the United States.

We reiterate our deep concern over the unprecedented frequency of ballistic missile launches conducted by the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea this year, particularly the launches involving intercontinental ballistic missiles on 24 March and just yesterday, on 25 May. These actions constitute flagrant violations of multiple Security Council resolutions, pose a serious threat to regional and international security, and undermine the global non-proliferation architecture.

Our positive vote is consistent with the Council’s established decisions, notably paragraph 28 of resolution 2397 (2017), which explicitly committed the Council to take further action in the event of a launch of a ballistic missile system of intercontinental range. The credibility of the Security Council depends on its willingness to follow through on its own decisions when the conditions it defined have materialized.

At the same time, Brazil has consistently emphasized that sanctions are not an end in themselves, but a tool to encourage compliance and foster the conditions for dialogue. We remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation of the North Korean civilian population, especially in light of the ongoing COVID-19 outbreak in the country. In this regard, we appreciated the inclusion of provisions in the draft resolution designed to facilitate and expedite humanitarian exemptions, ensuring that essential medical and humanitarian supplies could reach the population without impediment.

We must recognize, however, that sanctions alone cannot resolve the complex security dynamics on the Korean Peninsula. A sustainable and lasting solution will only be achieved through peaceful, diplomatic, and political means. Brazil urges all parties to exercise restraint, avoid actions that could further escalate tensions, and actively seek the resumption of meaningful, unconditional dialogue aimed at the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.

Finally, Brazil regrets that the Council was unable to speak with a united voice on this critical issue today.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.France:
France deeply regrets the result of today’s vote and the inability of the Security Council to adopt this draft resolution due to the vetoes cast by two permanent members.

Since the beginning of this year, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea has engaged in an unprecedented series of ballistic missile launches. The launches conducted on 24 March and just yesterday, on 25 May, involved intercontinental ballistic missiles. These tests are flagrant violations of Security Council resolutions. They represent a direct threat to regional stability and to international peace and security.

Faced with such severe and repeated provocations, the Council could not remain silent. In resolution 2397 (2017), adopted unanimously, the Council explicitly committed to take action and further restrict petroleum exports to the DPRK in the event of a nuclear test or an ICBM launch. Today’s draft resolution was the direct, legitimate, and necessary implementation of that commitment. 

By blocking the adoption of this text, the Council is failing to shoulder its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. This inaction sends a dangerous signal of division and emboldens the North Korean regime to continue developing its unlawful weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programmes with complete impunity. It also undermines the credibility of this Council and the global non-proliferation architecture.

France reaffirms that sanctions are not an end in themselves; they are an essential tool to constrain the proliferation programmes of the DPRK and to encourage Pyongyang to return to the negotiating table. We have consistently supported a diplomatic solution leading to the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula, in accordance with Council resolutions.

Finally, we emphasize that the draft resolution took full account of the humanitarian situation of the North Korean people, which has been exacerbated by the COVID-19 outbreak, by including clear provisions to streamline and expedite humanitarian exemptions. It is the North Korean authorities themselves who are depriving their population by prioritizing the development of illicit weapons over the welfare and health of their citizens.

France will remain firmly committed to the full implementation of existing Security Council resolutions and will continue to support all efforts to preserve peace, security, and the non-proliferation regime.
after.India:
Mr. President,

India has voted in favour of the draft resolution considered by the Council today.

India condemns the recent ballistic missile launches by the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, including the launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile on 25 May. These launches constitute a flagrant violation of relevant Security Council resolutions, undermine the global non-proliferation regime, and affect the peace and security of the region and beyond.

We call for the full implementation of all relevant Security Council resolutions relating to the DPRK. 

India also reiterates the pressing need to address the proliferation of nuclear and missile technologies related to the DPRK. The proliferation linkages connecting the DPRK’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes, including illicit transfers, are a matter of serious concern and have had a direct adverse impact on peace and security in our region.

India supports the complete denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula and reiterates its support for a peaceful resolution of all issues through dialogue and diplomacy.

Finally, we are mindful of the humanitarian situation in the DPRK, especially in the context of the recent reported outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic. In this regard, we take note of the provisions in the draft resolution that seek to ensure that humanitarian assistance and essential medical supplies are not adversely impacted and can reach the people of the DPRK.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Ireland:
Mr. President,

Ireland voted in favour of the draft resolution before us today, and we deeply regret that the Security Council has failed to adopt it due to the negative votes of two permanent members.

The Council cannot remain silent in the face of the DPRK’s repeated, reckless, and flagrant violations of Security Council resolutions. Since the beginning of this year, the DPRK has conducted an unprecedented number of ballistic missile launches, including tests of intercontinental ballistic missiles on 24 March and again just yesterday. These actions represent a grave escalation, pose a serious threat to regional and international peace and security, and undermine the global non-proliferation architecture.

In resolution 2397 (2017), adopted unanimously, this Council committed itself to take further action—specifically to further restrict petroleum exports—in the event of a further ICBM launch by the DPRK. By failing to adopt today’s text, the Council has failed to uphold its own clear commitment and has sent the wrong message to Pyongyang.

Ireland remains acutely concerned by the dire humanitarian situation in the DPRK, which is now further exacerbated by the reported outbreak of COVID-19. We are steadfast in our conviction that sanctions should not cause unintended negative humanitarian consequences for the civilian population. For that reason, Ireland welcomed the clear and robust humanitarian safeguards included in today’s draft resolution, particularly measures aimed at expediting and facilitating humanitarian exemptions for essential medical supplies and life-saving aid.

We urge the DPRK to immediately cease all destabilizing actions, to comply fully with its obligations under relevant Security Council resolutions, and to return to the path of dialogue and diplomacy. The only viable path to sustainable peace and security on the Korean Peninsula is through dialogue towards complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Mexico:
Mr. President,

Mexico voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted today by the United States. 

Our vote is consistent with Mexico’s foreign policy principles, our unwavering commitment to nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation, and our consistent condemnation of the repeated launches of ballistic missiles by the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, including the intercontinental ballistic missiles launched on 24 March and just yesterday, 25 May. 

These actions constitute flagrant violations of multiple Security Council resolutions, undermine the global non-proliferation regime, heighten regional tensions, and pose a grave threat to international peace and security.

Mexico regrets that the Council was unable to adopt this draft resolution. In resolution 2397 (2017), adopted unanimously, the Council explicitly decided that if the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea conducted a further launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile, the Council would take action to further restrict petroleum exports. The Council's credibility is eroded when it fails to respond collectively and effectively to clear breaches of its own decisions and to commitments previously agreed by all of its members.

At the same time, we wish to reiterate that sanctions are not an end in themselves. They are an instrument under the Charter to incentivize compliance with international law and facilitate political solutions. We welcomed the fact that the text put to the vote contained provisions aimed at safeguarding humanitarian assistance, which is particularly vital at this time given the severe public health challenges and the COVID-19 outbreak affecting the civilian population in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea. The international community must remain attentive to the humanitarian needs of the North Korean people and ensure that humanitarian exemptions operate expeditiously.

Finally, Mexico reiterates that the only viable path to lasting peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula is through diplomacy and dialogue. We urge the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea to cease all provocations, fully comply with relevant Security Council resolutions, and return to negotiations without preconditions, in order to advance towards the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Norway:
Norway voted in favour of the draft resolution today, and we deeply regret that the Security Council failed to adopt it and was unable to speak with one voice.

The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea has conducted an unprecedented number of ballistic missile launches this year, including launches of intercontinental ballistic missiles, most recently just yesterday. These actions are in flagrant violation of multiple Security Council resolutions, pose a grave threat to regional and international peace and security, and undermine the global non-proliferation architecture.

In resolution 2397 (2017), this Council clearly committed itself to take further action to restrict petroleum exports to the DPRK if it were to conduct further ICBM launches. The Security Council has a responsibility to follow through on its own decisions. Today’s draft resolution was a necessary, measured, and calibrated response to the DPRK’s ongoing violations and escalatory behaviour.

Norway also welcomed that the draft resolution took carefully into account the humanitarian situation in the DPRK, including explicit provisions to facilitate humanitarian assistance and humanitarian exemptions, which are all the more urgent in light of the reported COVID-19 outbreak in the country.

Council unity has been essential in addressing the DPRK’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. Today's failure to act undermines the credibility of the Security Council and sends a dangerous signal. 

We reiterate our call on the DPRK to cease all destabilizing actions, comply fully with its obligations under relevant Security Council resolutions, and engage in meaningful dialogue toward the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted against the draft resolution submitted by the United States on the imposition of additional sanctions against the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.

We have repeatedly stated, and we reiterate today, that the path of tightening sanctions pressure on Pyongyang is a complete dead end. Over many years, the introduction of ever new restrictive measures has proven to be absolutely ineffective in achieving the proclaimed goals of resolving the nuclear issue on the Korean Peninsula and ensuring security in the region. On the contrary, continuing to ramp up sanctions pressure not only threatens to push the situation on the Korean Peninsula into a dangerous escalation, but also carries grave humanitarian consequences for the civilian population of the DPRK, particularly at a time when the country is confronting a difficult epidemiological situation related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

We cannot ignore the fact that for several years, the DPRK observed a self-imposed moratorium on nuclear and intercontinental ballistic missile tests and dismantled its nuclear test site. In each of its resolutions, the Security Council committed to review the restrictive measures in light of the DPRK’s compliance. Yet, the Council completely ignored these positive signals, failing to take even a single step towards easing restrictions or meeting Pyongyang halfway. Instead, our Western colleagues have consistently demanded unilateral concessions from the DPRK, while offering nothing in return and continuing their military exercises and sanctions pressure, thereby escalating tensions.

The problems of the Korean Peninsula cannot be resolved without addressing the legitimate security concerns of the DPRK. A sustainable settlement can be achieved exclusively through political and diplomatic means, through equal, mutually respectful dialogue and the gradual, step-by-step easing of tensions.

It is precisely to this end that Russia and China prepared and circulated a draft resolution in the Security Council aimed at improving the humanitarian situation in the DPRK and creating the necessary conditions to restart political dialogue. Regrettably, the penholders completely disregarded our constructive proposals and preferred instead to push through a divisive draft focused solely on expanding sanctions.

Under these circumstances, we could not support this draft resolution, which is completely counterproductive and disconnected from reality. We call on our partners to abandon the flawed logic of escalating sanctions and confrontation and to return to joint work on political and diplomatic solutions.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The United Arab Emirates voted in favour of the draft resolution today. Our vote reflects our firm commitment to the global non-proliferation regime, as well as our conviction that the credibility and authority of the Security Council and its resolutions must be upheld.

The DPRK’s persistent and unprecedented launches of ballistic missiles this year, including intercontinental ballistic missiles, represent flagrant violations of multiple Security Council resolutions and pose a serious threat to regional and international peace and security. In resolution 2397 (2017), this Council explicitly committed to taking further action in the event of an ICBM launch. In the face of repeated, deliberate non-compliance, the Council has a clear responsibility to respond.

At the same time, the UAE firmly believes that a sustainable resolution to the situation on the Korean Peninsula can only be achieved through peaceful, diplomatic, and political means. We urge the DPRK to comply with its international obligations, cease its destabilizing actions, and return to meaningful and unconditional dialogue towards the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula.

We also remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation and the reports of an escalating COVID-19 outbreak in the DPRK. For this reason, we welcomed the draft resolution’s explicit provisions aimed at safeguarding humanitarian assistance and ensuring that measures adopted by this Council do not adversely impact the civilian population.

The UAE will continue to support all constructive efforts aimed at de-escalation, dialogue, and maintaining peace and stability in Northeast Asia.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom voted in favour of today’s draft resolution, and we deeply regret that the Security Council has failed to adopt it due to the vetoes cast by China and the Russian Federation.

Yesterday, the DPRK launched an intercontinental ballistic missile alongside two other ballistic missiles. This brings the total number of ballistic missile launches conducted by the DPRK this year to over twenty. Each of these launches constitutes a flagrant violation of multiple Security Council resolutions and represents a direct and increasing threat to international peace and security.

In resolution 2397 (2017), adopted unanimously, this Council clearly and explicitly decided that should the DPRK conduct a launch of an intercontinental ballistic missile, the Council would take action to further restrict petroleum exports to the DPRK. The draft resolution put forward today by the United States followed through directly on that commitment. It was a measured, appropriate, and necessary response to the DPRK’s repeated and dangerous provocations.

Thirteen members of this Council voted in favour of this text, demonstrating overwhelming support for upholding the Council’s credibility and the global non-proliferation architecture. By choosing to veto this resolution, China and Russia have failed in their responsibility as permanent members to maintain international peace and security. They have chosen to shield the DPRK regime from accountability, sending a dangerous signal of tolerance for unlawful proliferation.

Sanctions are not an end in themselves; they are designed to constrain the DPRK’s illicit weapons programmes and bring Pyongyang back to the negotiating table. We have consistently made clear that the Council’s measures do not target the people of North Korea, and the draft resolution included robust provisions to facilitate humanitarian assistance, which is especially vital given the grave COVID-19 outbreak currently reported in the country. It is the DPRK regime itself that continues to divert scarce resources away from its people’s urgent humanitarian needs to fund its unlawful weapons programmes.

The United Kingdom remains steadfast in its commitment to the complete, verifiable, and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula. We call on the DPRK to cease its destabilizing actions, comply fully with its international obligations, and take up the repeated offers of dialogue. In the meantime, we urge all Member States to fully and strictly implement all existing Security Council resolutions.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President.

I want to thank the 12 Council members who joined the United States today in voting in favor of this resolution. Thirteen members of this Council stood together to defend the global non-proliferation regime, uphold Council resolutions, and hold the DPRK accountable for its dangerous, unlawful, and escalatory actions.

We are deeply disappointed that today, for the first time in 15 years, a Council member has used the veto to stop the Council from holding the DPRK accountable for its repeated, flagrant violations of international law. In this case, two permanent members chose to shield the DPRK and provide it with cover, rather than hold it responsible for threatening international peace and security.

Let us be completely clear about what happened today. In 2017, this Council unanimously adopted resolution 2397. In paragraph 28 of that resolution, every member of this Council—including China and the Russian Federation—agreed that if the DPRK conducted an ICBM launch, the Council would take action to further restrict petroleum exports to the DPRK. 

The DPRK has launched multiple ICBMs this year, including just yesterday. The draft resolution we voted on today was a direct fulfillment of the Council’s own unanimous commitment. Yet today, China and Russia walked away from their own words and their own commitments, effectively giving Pyongyang a blank check to continue its unlawful weapons development.

We have heard some Council members claim that additional sanctions would worsen the humanitarian situation or that the Council should pursue dialogue. The draft resolution we voted on today contained clear, robust, and expedited humanitarian exemptions, specifically tailored to assist the North Korean people, especially in the midst of a grave COVID-19 outbreak. It is the DPRK regime itself that chooses to divert resources from its people to its ballistic missile and nuclear programs, and it is the DPRK’s self-imposed border closures that restrict aid.

Furthermore, the United States has repeatedly stated, publicly and privately, that we are prepared to engage in serious and sustained diplomacy without preconditions. We have reached out to Pyongyang directly, offering humanitarian assistance and dialogue. Those calls have been met only with missile launches and deafening silence.

Today’s vetoes do not reflect a failure of the resolution; they reflect a failure of two permanent members to shoulder their responsibilities under the UN Charter. They send a dangerous signal to proliferators around the world that they can violate international norms with impunity if they have powerful protectors on this Council.

The United States will not stand by while the DPRK threatens our allies and international peace and security. We will continue to work closely with our partners, allies, and the overwhelming majority of the international community to fully enforce existing Security Council resolutions, protect our collective security, and hold the DPRK accountable.

Thank you, Mr. President.
